title: fix(plugin-grid,plugin-list): resolve context tokens in a directly authored object-grid or list-view filter (objectui#10607)
body:
Fixes #10607
Clause-②: no — the documented context tokens resolve on two more hosts, through the one shared resolver; no schema, export or accept set moves.

## What changed

A directly authored `object-grid` or `list-view` node, with no `object-view` above it, sent `filter: [['owner', '=', '{current_user_id}']]` on `$filter` as the literal token. Neither `plugin-grid` nor `plugin-list` read `resolveFilterPlaceholders` or `useFilterScope`. Each host now resolves its own authored filter ONCE, through `@object-ui/core`'s shared `resolveFilterPlaceholders`, against `useFilterScope()` from `@object-ui/react`. This is the shape PR objectui#10577 used for `object-view`. There is no second resolver, and neither `filter-tokens.ts` nor `useFilterScope.ts` is touched.

**The hold.** It is the pattern of plugin-view's `useResolvedFilterSegments`, one per host. The resolved value is held in state, keyed on the authored filter (compared by structure) and on the scope's three members (`currentUserId`, `currentOrgId`, `onUnresolved`), each compared on its own and never by the scope object's identity (AGENTS.md #10). A set during render re-resolves when an input changes. Each host has one resolved value, and every read site reads it.

- **`@object-ui/plugin-grid`, `ObjectGrid`.** `useResolvedGridFilters` resolves the node's `filter` and its deprecated alias `defaultFilters` in one call.
  - `schemaFilterSource` (the lowering both the query and the server-side export read) now reads the resolved `filter`.
  - The load effect's `defaultFilters` leg reads the resolved alias.
  - The load effect now also lists the resolved alias (`schemaDefaultFilters`). It read `schema.defaultFilters` without keying on it, so a new signed-in user would not have re-queried a token carried only there.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-list`, `ListView`.** `useResolvedAuthoredFilter` resolves `schema.filter` once, right after the schema is normalized. The fetch and its dependency list, the page-reset signature, the self-querying views (gantt, tree, chart), the child view's node (`filter:`), the export and its dependency list, and the empty-state "filtered" test all read `authoredFilter`. After this change the only raw `schema.filter` read left in code is the hold's own input.
- **The comparator.** `isSameAuthoredFilter` sits in each file. It follows the same rules as plugin-view's `isStructurallyEqual`: primitives by `Object.is`, a `Date` by instant, arrays in order, plain objects by key set, and everything else by reference. It is local because plugin-view depends on plugin-grid, plugin-list depends on neither, and a shared export would move an export set.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/10607-grid-list-filter-context-tokens.md`, with `'@object-ui/plugin-grid': patch` and `'@object-ui/plugin-list': patch`. One sentence of the pending `.changeset/10506-named-view-context-tokens.md` is corrected too (round 2, below).

**Round 2 (`80eca8f`, on amended claim 5834409941).** Prose only.
- `.changeset/10506-named-view-context-tokens.md`: one sentence, and the front matter is byte-identical (md5 `8212bf42dc2f6ba4025ef7ced79c6d6d` before and after). 「(A directly authored `object-grid` or `list-view` node still does not call it.)」 becomes 「(A directly authored `object-grid` or `list-view` node calls it too, since objectui#10607.)」.
- This PR's changeset: the sentence that pointed at the gap the 10506 entry used to note now reads "`object-view` has done this since objectui#10506; these two nodes, authored directly, had not."
- Merged `origin/main` `f99f9cd` (plugin-form only), with no conflict. Between `e4aa578` and `80eca8f`, no file under `packages/plugin-grid` or `packages/plugin-list` changes.

- At `80eca8f`, each exit 0: `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-overwrite` (1 added, 1 modified: the 10506 file, declaring `plugin-view: patch` and `core: patch` at base and now), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:control-bytes` and `check:new-line-citations` (0 new).

## Measured

The code was measured at `e4aa578`, which is the merge of `origin/main` `4a3d500` into the branch. The branch was cut at `dddbc27`. Round 2 then merged `origin/main` `f99f9cd` (plugin-form only) and changed no code in either package; its own readings are in the Round 2 paragraph below.

**The pins.** Each renders the registered node under `FilterScopeProvider` (user `usr_42`, org `org_7`) and reads `dataSource.find`'s `$filter`.

- The grid pin has 10 cells:
  - `{current_user_id}` and `{current_org_id}`.
  - The `defaultFilters` alias.
  - A token-free CONTROL.
  - No scope: the token stays literal and the resolver warns.
  - A user change re-queries, both on `filter` and on `defaultFilters` alone.
  - The count holds across same-node re-renders, and across re-renders that rebuild an equal filter.
  - The object-view seam: a filter already resolved upstream is queried once, unchanged.
- The list pin has 9 cells: the same set, with the child view's handed filter in place of the alias cells.

| run | grid pin | list pin |
|---|---|---|
| base: each source swapped to its `4a3d500` blob, the pins as committed | 7 failed, 3 passed (exit 1) | 6 failed, 3 passed (exit 1) |
| head `e4aa578` | 10 passed | 9 passed (both files in one run: 19 passed, exit 0) |

On base, the token cells fail reading the literal (`expected [ [ 'owner', '=', '{current_user_id}' ] ] …`). The cells that pass on base are the CONTROL, the same-node count and the already-resolved seam, as they should.

**H4, the hold, by ablation.** `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode swapped each hold call for a bare per-render `resolveFilterPlaceholders(…)`. The anchor hit once, and the blob moved.

- Grid: `5 failed | 5 passed`. The five hold cells time out at 15000ms: a copy minted every render re-queries without end. The five token cells stay green.
- List: `4 failed | 5 passed`. Two cells time out at 15000ms. Two read `expected 0 to be greater than 0`: no `find()` landed inside the 1000ms wait while the list kept re-rendering.
- Both restored: `blob after restore` equals `blob at HEAD`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- The pins import the subject from `src/` (`../index`, `../ListView`), so no `dist/` leg exists here.

**H3, the object-view path, measured once and not kept as a file.** A temporary plugin-view test drove the real `ObjectView` into the real `ObjectGrid` under the same scope, then re-rendered twice (the same schema, then a spread copy).

| case | head: fetches | base `ObjectGrid.tsx`: fetches | `$filter` (identical in both) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table.filter` | 1, then 1 | 1, then 1 | `[["owner","=","usr_42"]]` |
| named grid view (reaches the grid as `defaultFilters`) | 1, then 1 | 1, then 1 | `[["owner","equals","usr_42"]]` |

Resolving twice is a no-op, and it adds no fetch. The base file was swapped in and restored with a hash check against HEAD. The temporary test was deleted, and `git status` is clean.

- `check:new-line-citations` (0 new) and `check:pending-changeset-literals`.

**The changeset-claims gate** (`check:changeset-claims`) is report-only and exited 0. It lists 12 pending changesets that name `ObjectGrid.tsx` or `ListView.tsx`. Each paragraph was re-read, and none concerns the filter read: they cover i18n keys, `reference_to`, gantt date fields, export options, kanban `groupField` and record source, the bulk executor's data source, the page size, `userActions`, and comment corrections.

**eslint** on the four changed files, plain form: exit 0, 0 errors.
- Warnings per rule, `4a3d500` against head, are unchanged in both sources: `ObjectGrid.tsx` 207 → 207 and `ListView.tsx` 184 → 184, with 0 rules differing.
- The two pins have 0 findings.

**NOT MEASURED:**
- `check:eager-closure` and `check:sdui-registration-pins`. Both need a full `@object-ui/console` production build; the second exits 2 ("No console build to weigh"), which is a missing prerequisite, not a verdict. CI's Bundle Analysis runs them. The only new import is `resolveFilterPlaceholders` from `@object-ui/core`, which the console already loads eagerly through its app-shell callers.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full test farm belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **The pending objectui#10506 changeset** said a directly authored `object-grid` or `list-view` node still did not call the resolver. That was false once this PR lands, so round 2 corrects that one sentence (see Round 2). `check:changeset-claims` would not have flagged it, because it names the symbols, not the files.
- **Fewer queries, by design.** On base both hosts keyed their fetch on the filter's identity, so a host that rebuilt an equal filter inline re-queried on every render. The structural hold now drops those redundant queries, and pins them in the equal-filter cells. A structurally different filter, or a new scope member, still re-queries.
- **The object-view named-view grid, a source reading, not measured.** `ObjectView` hands a named view's filter to `ObjectGrid` in `defaultFilters`. It re-resolves that filter when the user changes, and it does not remount the grid (its key carries no user). On base the grid's load effect did not key on `defaultFilters`, so it did not re-query in place. The new `schemaDefaultFilters` dependency covers that too.
- **Date macros** (`{today}`, …) are now resolved on the client for these two nodes, in the browser's local time. That is the same call `object-view`, the app-shell host, `ObjectChart` and the dashboards make. Before, they reached the server as literals, and the ObjectStack server resolved them in the tenant's configured `localization.timezone` (UTC by default). A browser whose local day differs from the server's can now get a different day. They are held until the scope or the filter changes, so a refetch for another reason reuses the held value.
- **Against ObjectStack**, the server also expands `{current_user_id}` for a signed-in request, and refuses the request otherwise. So this is defence in depth there (triage graded it p3), and a real gap on a backend with no resolver of its own.
- **Unchanged here, pre-existing.** `ObjectGrid`'s load effect still keys on `schemaFilter`, which comes out of a `useMemo` (`toFilterNodeSafely`). That is an identity dependency AGENTS.md #10 names, and this PR feeds it a held input without moving it. `ListView`'s `selfQueryFilterRef` (a JSON-key hold) is also unchanged, and it now receives the resolved filter.
- **Prose elsewhere.** `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` lists the resolver's callers without these two hosts. The list is now incomplete, but it is not false, and no docs sentence states that these two hosts skip the resolver.
- **Overlap.** objectui#10620 landed on `ListView.tsx` during this run. The merge conflicted in two places, both inside this PR's hunks, and was resolved as a union: the `@object-ui/react` import keeps `useDataInvalidation` and adds `useFilterScope`, and the fetch effect's dependency list keeps `invalidationNonce` and reads `authoredFilter`. objectui#10278 (a draft on the `ObjectGrid` page size) touches other regions.
